Worked like a charm! - This dryer duct cleaner was about as easy to use and worked as well as you could ask for. The segments are flexible enough to bend around 90 degree corners no problem, though it did take a little bit of finessing to get it around an S-bend in my duct. The kit seems pretty durable, and I don't forsee any issues getting several annual cleanings. 12' was not quite long enough to get my whole duct, but working from each end using a shop vac to assist (see below) took me all of maybe 20 minutes once I got the dryer moved.

In addition to following the instructions about removing the outside vent cap, I found it worked well to stick the blower hose of my shop vac into the dryer end of the duct and blow air through the duct as I worked the rotary brush through. (Just make sure to use a rag or blanket to seal up the end you're working from, so the air is actually forced through the duct) With the shop vac going, and working about 12" at a time, I ended up with a pretty good pile of lint outside that had been cleaned out!

The instructions say to wrap each joint with a piece of duct tape--that's probably a good idea, but as long as you're careful to ONLY rotate the brush clockwise, you will actually be tightening the threaded joints. Another reviewer mentioned setting the clutch on your electric drill to the lowest setting--also a very good idea, just in case the brush were to get caught on a sharp edge of duct or something.

Metal filter doesn’t work - Pros:
- Collapses very small so I can take it with me anywhere, also quite light
- Silicone is washable and reusable
- Does hold its form while brewing

Cons:
- Despite the air hole, can develop a seal to the cup
- Can’t see through it to tell how far along the cup is
- A little dangerous to lift it up while brewing to check fill level, since it’s squishy
- Metal filter will either pop out of place, sending the entire filter full of grounds into your cup, or (if you’re very lucky) stay put and only allow about 1/3 cup to brew before clogging. This is when using beans ground to the “drip” setting by my local roaster. May have better luck with coarser grounds.

Overall assessment:
Not annoying enough to replace, but annoying enough that I won’t recommend it. If you do choose to buy this, use with paper filters.

Good luck - This was an easy repair, but can be a bit nervy as you have to be very careful when changing it out. First, you need to be absolutely sure that your frig is out of warranty (yes, this is the one time you should have purchased that extened warranty). Be sure the installed unit is completely deforsted using the force defrost mode or shut ot down for 24 hours. Ensure the ice make is completely free of ice. Remove the harness trim and disconnect the wiring harness. You then need to remove the set screw and detent tab to drop down the bottom half of the component. If this doesn't make any sense to you stop here and call a professional. If you're tracking thus far carefully pull down the lower half and depress the upper tab to free the unit, then slide the ice maker out from around the coil (if you damage this coil just push you refrigerator to the curb for trash pick up, because it'll cost more to fix it than to buy another one). If you manage to get this far, use some food grade silicone to seal up the comparment as this is most likely why you ice make compartment frosted up and damaged your ice maker (there are some youtube videos for this). Next install the new ice maker ensuring that the pads between the halves are aligned with the coil. Close everything back up. If this is outside your wheel house just pay the repairman their blood money. If they properly seal the compartment and don't damage anything during the installation of the new ice maker you shouldn't have any problems with your frig for a long time. Keep in mind that Samsung doesn't own the rights to bad ice make designs as the ice maker is usually the thing that causes the most problems for every brand. Our previous refrigerator was a Frigidaire and was so bad that we threw in the towel (boxing term for forfeiture because the boxer has been injuried soo badly that even they no longer can precieve that they should quit and their manager makes the call). Good luck.

3. It has a disco looking two steps blue light inside, but it’s not door sensitive, so I can’t figure out when I will ever turn it on?
4. It comes with hardware so you can change to door to open on left hand side.
5. The noise level is acceptable. I can hear it, but not loud enough to bother me. The cooler is open space kitchen bar area.
6. It was delivered double boxed. With the exception of bended shelfs, there is no dent to the body.
7. The price I paid was about 1/3 of an U-Line. I purchased a three years extended warranty, so, if it lasts five years, I’m happy.

The bottom line is level your expectation and you get what you paid for.
